task: Sourcing-only. No files wired in; nothing edited outside scratch/.

currentPlate.title: Auckland Domain where the cricket ground is
currentPlate.artist: Kennett Watkins (c. 1890), Auckland War Memorial Museum Tamaki Paenga Hira (PD-1996-1-3)
currentPlate.note: Excluded from candidates. It is an illustration (a Watkins painting of Auckland Domain), not a photograph, so it satisfies the illustration rule; this task looks for a stronger, more identifiably-Auckland harbour/townscape alternative.

selectionRules: Must depict Auckland as an actual place (harbour / townscape / Rangitoto / Waitemata).
Public domain or CC0/CC-BY with attribution.
Colour preferred where a good colour option exists.

candidates.title: Rangitoto & part of Auckland harbour (Judge's Bay)
candidates.collection: Hocken Collections, Uare Taoka o Hakena, University of Otago (Dr T.M. Hocken's Collection)
candidates.borderOrMount: Very thin off-white paper margin only; a light edge crop tidies it, no heavy trimming needed.
candidates.fitNote: Iconic, well-preserved colour view over Waitemata Harbour to Rangitoto Island, with waka/canoes and figures on the beach and cattle in the foreground; unmistakably Auckland. Best all-round fit despite being just under the 1200px target.

candidates.title: North Head and Rangitoto
candidates.borderOrMount: Yes. Mounted on brown card with a visible paper edge and pencil caption; needs trimming to the painted area.
candidates.fitNote: Delicate colour watercolour of North Head with Rangitoto beyond and a moored boat; clearly Auckland's Waitemata approaches. Good resolution but requires a mount crop and is compositionally quieter than the Fox.

candidates.title: Auckland, New Zealand in 1853
candidates.collection: Auckland War Memorial Museum Tamaki Paenga Hira (ref. PD-1985-1-25)
candidates.license: Public domain / No known copyright restrictions
candidates.borderOrMount: Yes, heavy. Photographed inside a large ornate gilt frame and cream mount; the actual painting occupies only the central ~40 percent and must be cropped out.
candidates.fitNote: Charming colour oil of the Auckland waterfront and harbour with shipping and foreground figures. Very high source resolution, but the frame crop leaves a smaller usable image (~roughly 900px wide once trimmed).

candidates.title: Auckland Waterfront
candidates.artist: Charles Heaphy (artwork); photographed by James D. Richardson
candidates.collection: Auckland Libraries / Auckland City Heritage Images
candidates.medium: Watercolour / wash drawing (reproduced as a monochrome photograph)
candidates.borderOrMount: No mount; faint tonal edges from the photographic reproduction only.
candidates.fitNote: Detailed, historically rich Auckland waterfront townscape (wharves, sailmaker, hotel, church on the ridge), and by a named artist requested in the brief. Rejected as top pick only because the surviving reproduction is monochrome and faded, and the brief prefers colour.

candidates.title: From near Auckland
candidates.borderOrMount: Full sketchbook page with large blank yellowed margins; would need heavy cropping to the small landscape band at the bottom.
candidates.fitNote: Faint, sparse field study of a distant Auckland settlement across water. Weakest option: mostly empty paper, low colour saturation, and little detail once cropped.

recommendation.reason: Best combination of the brief's requirements: a strong colour illustration, unmistakably Auckland (Waitemata Harbour with Rangitoto), well preserved and complete, public domain, and needs almost no trimming. If a larger asset is essential, the Abraham watercolour (1600x954) is the runner-up but needs a mount crop and is a quieter composition.

round2.task: Round 2 sourcing-only pass. Wider net across open collections for NEW, distinct COLOUR illustrations of Auckland. Nothing wired in; nothing edited outside scratch/.
round2.note: All six below are NEW files, distinct from the round-1 set. All are colour illustrations (no photographs) and public domain. Downscaled to 1500px long edge with macOS sips.

candidates.title: Queen Street, Auckland
candidates.collection: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tamaki (via Google Art Project / Google Cultural Institute, asset OAHFvUTHUA75Sg)
candidates.license: Public domain (PD-Art; artist died 1933, work out of copyright; Google reproduction PD)
candidates.borderOrMount: No. Painted to the edges; only the artist's signature sits in the lower-right corner. No trimming needed.
candidates.fitNote: Superb, richly detailed colour street view straight up Queen Street with the Post Office clock tower, Anderson's Imperial Hotel, horse traffic and figures; the most unmistakably-Auckland city scene of the whole set and by far the highest-quality option.

candidates.title: First Government House, Auckland
candidates.collection: Alexander Turnbull Library / National Library of New Zealand (record 23035127)
candidates.borderOrMount: No mount; only a thin off-white paper margin, a light edge crop tidies it.
candidates.fitNote: Clean, well-preserved colour watercolour of the first Government House with a volcanic cone (Maungawhau / Mount Eden direction) behind; strong resolution and true Auckland subject, though it reads as a building-in-landscape rather than a harbour panorama.

candidates.title: Auckland, from the Verandah of Mr Reader Wood's Cottage
candidates.collection: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tamaki (via Google Art Project / Google Cultural Institute, asset KgETpsNOnUzW0Q)
candidates.borderOrMount: Thin paper margin with a pencil caption at the foot; a light crop tidies it.
candidates.fitNote: Atmospheric colour watercolour by a named brief artist (Kinder), looking out through a verandah over rolling country to the distant harbour; beautiful but portrait-shaped and the harbour is a faint distant band, so it is less immediately readable as Auckland.

candidates.title: Queen Street, Auckland, 1843
candidates.collection: Auckland War Memorial Museum Tamaki Paenga Hira (ref. PD-1965-20), via Auckland Museum Flickr
candidates.license: Public domain / No known copyright restrictions (PD-old-70)
candidates.resolution: 1500x1000 as downloaded (from 6000x4000), but the painting itself occupies only the central ~55 percent
candidates.borderOrMount: Yes, heavy. Photographed on its original card mount with a printed title strip and pencil annotations; must be cropped hard to the painted area (usable image roughly 900px wide once trimmed).
candidates.fitNote: Historically precious pioneer view of Queen Street as a raw settlement above the harbour; earliest and most documentary Auckland option, but pale/faded and needs an aggressive mount crop.

candidates.title: A Golden Eve, Waiheke Island
candidates.collection: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tamaki (via Google Art Project / Google Cultural Institute, asset 4AGxvu1CBQsDKw)
candidates.borderOrMount: No mount; thin paper margin only.
candidates.fitNote: Gorgeous, high-resolution golden-hour bush landscape in the Auckland region (Waiheke, Hauraki Gulf), but it depicts generic native forest with no harbour, city or Rangitoto cue, so it does not read as identifiably Auckland per rule 1; include only as an evocative regional fallback.

candidates.title: Panoramic view of Waitemata Harbour looking westward from the summit of Rangitoto
candidates.collection: Auckland War Memorial Museum Tamaki Paenga Hira, via Auckland Museum Flickr
candidates.license: Public domain / No known copyright restrictions (PD-New Zealand)
candidates.resolution: 1500x1000 as downloaded, but framed; the painted strip is a very wide ~4:1 band inside the mount
candidates.borderOrMount: Yes, heavy. Photographed inside a timber frame and wide cream mount against black cloth; must crop out the frame/mount to the thin panoramic strip.
candidates.fitNote: Rare 1843 harbour panorama from the summit of Rangitoto, but faded, extreme letterbox aspect ratio, and dominated by frame/mount; awkward to fit a pin and weakest of the six.

recommendation.reason: Jacques Carabain's 1889 Queen Street oil is the standout of both rounds: a large (6725x5150 source), vivid, well-preserved colour cityscape that is instantly recognisable as Auckland (Queen Street, Post Office clock tower), needs no trimming, and is clearly public domain. If a watercolour or a quieter view is preferred over an oil street scene, Edward Ashworth's First Government House (5311x3256 source, clean margins, PD via the Turnbull Library) is the best runner-up. The round-1 Fox 1856 Rangitoto harbour view remains the best pure harbour-and-Rangitoto option if a water/island composition is wanted instead.
